---
title: "Exercise 2.2"
---


## Solution

Consider $X=\{1,2,3,4\}$, and 
$$\mathcal{A}_1 = \{\emptyset, \{1\},\{2,3,4\},X\}, \quad \mathcal{A}_2 = \{\emptyset, \{1,2,3\},\{4\},X\}. $$

It is straightforward to verify that $\mathcal{A}_1$ and $\mathcal{A}_2$ are $\sigma$-algebras.
However, $\mathcal{A}_1\cup\mathcal{A}_2$
is not a $\sigma$-algebra, since

$$ \{1\} \cup \{4\} = \{1,4\} \notin  \mathcal{A}_1\cup\mathcal{A}_2.$$
